Surreptitious

sur-up-TISH-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Surreptitious is kept secret, especially because it would not be approved of.

The cat made a surreptitious approach toward the fish tank whenever it thought no one was watching.

Worked Example

The student took a surreptitious peek at his neighbor's answer sheet while pretending to stretch.

Surreptitious describes an action done secretly, specifically to avoid being noticed or caught.

How Surreptitious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

sneaky

sneaky: the everyday word for doing something on the sly; surreptitious is the formal word for secrecy meant to escape notice

stealthy

stealthy: careful and quiet to avoid being noticed

Antonyms

open

open: not secretive or hidden

overt

overt: done or shown openly

How Strong Is It? — quiet → surreptitious → underhanded

quiet vs. surreptitious

quiet vs. surreptitious: Quiet simply means not loud; surreptitious specifically implies intentional secrecy to avoid detection.

underhanded vs. surreptitious

underhanded vs. surreptitious: Underhanded goes further than surreptitious, adding a clearly dishonest or unfair motive to the secrecy.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of surreptitious.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — sur-

prefix — sur-: under, secretly (Latin (sub-))

root — rept

root — rept: to seize (Latin (rapere))

suffix — -itious

suffix — -itious: full of, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: sur- ('secretly, under') + rept ('to seize') + -itious together trace back to 'seizing secretly' -- exactly the sneaky, hidden action surreptitious describes.

Use the root in a new word: usurp

Use the root in a new word: usurp: Usurp shares the same Latin root rapere ('to seize'), taught earlier in Unit 47 -- though usurp specifically means to seize power or a position.
